mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the Federal Funds rate above 4% in the month prior to the decision is associated with a short-term negative S&P 500 20-day forward return due to higher discounting of future cash flows.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 4% in the prior month
regime_hint: tightening cycle after a period of easing
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero when FEDFUNDS > 4% in prior month (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment claims (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signal a weakening labor market and supply-side pressure, leading to negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases while INDPRO decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant (t-test p < 0.05) during such labor market conditions.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly increase in home sales (HOUST) above 2% suggests strengthening consumer demand, which is associated with a positive S&P 20-day forward return.
failure_condition: Over 12 consecutive months of rising HOUST > 2%, 20-day forward returns show no outperformance vs. a flat macro backdrop (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in industrial production (INDPRO) for three consecutive months predicts a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to reduced future earnings expectations.
failure_condition: INDPRO recovers sharply in the following month with 20-day forward returns turning positive and statistically significant.

mechanism_narrative: When consumer price inflation (CPIAUCSL) exceeds 3% for two consecutive months, the S&P 60-day forward return is expected to be negative due to preemptive rate hike anticipation.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 3% and remains above for two months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with p > 0.05 during such inflation spikes.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in unemployment (UNRATE) and a decline in manufacturing payrolls (not available, so use PAYEMS drop) indicates labor market stress, resulting in a negative 20-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases while PAYEMS decreases in the same month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive and statistically significant when UNRATE falls and PAYEMS falls together.

mechanism_narrative: A monthly surge in retail employment (PAYEMS > 150,000) combined with a drop in industrial production (INDPRO) suggests demand shift without supply response, predicting a positive 5-day forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS crosses above 150,000 while INDPRO falls in the same month
failure_condition: 5-day forward return is not positive or is negative with p < 0.05 during such events.

mechanism_narrative: A prolonged decline in consumer demand proxies (GDPC1 over three months) is associated with a negative S&P 20-day forward return due to lower earnings expectations.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not negative or are positive with p > 0.05 during three-month GDPC1 decline.
